scope: Immediate account-to-account transfer HTTP commands and owned reads, durable scoped idempotency, cross-process spending concurrency, and uncertain-response recovery. Asynchronous payments, RabbitMQ workers, adjustments, schedules, webhooks and React remain later phases.

requirements.statement: Authenticated CUSTOMER commands create one immediate same-currency transfer through the protected PostgreSQL command path and return the durable receipt, Location and replay indicator.
Actor/kind/key scope and canonical normalized intent provide exact replay while changed economically meaningful intent returns 409 without another financial effect.
Concurrent identical requests through independent API processes produce one transfer, one journal and one durable outcome.
The canonical 10000 available versus two synchronized 8000 requests across API processes permits exactly one success and no negative balance, leaked hold or duplicate journal.
A response deliberately dropped only after the API completed its commit becomes an uncertain client outcome; replaying the same key and intent returns the original transfer with one committed effect.
Missing/malformed keys and malformed, mass-assigned or unowned intents are rejected before idempotency claim; customer reads are owner-scoped and counterparty-private.
Deterministic insufficient-funds, self-transfer, cross-currency and closed-recipient outcomes are atomic; accepted rejection replay is stable and does not create postings.
Opposite-direction operations follow stable lock order, many clients cannot overspend one account, and independent accounts can progress concurrently.
Restricted runtime credentials cannot forge transfer rows, and current CUSTOMER/CSRF authorization protects transfer commands while ADMIN cannot spend as a customer.
The current P04 OpenAPI and TypeScript client describe/use exact string money, owner read paths and persistent uncertain intents without silently generating a new key.
